# Official store 2.5.0, native durability repair

Source: https://crates.io/crates/tauri-plugin-store/2.5.0
Release: https://github.com/tauri-apps/plugins-workspace/releases/tag/store-v2.5.0
Upstream commit: a2364a5f216324439feedeb25b2db74e7b1eba90 (`plugins/store`).
Published archive SHA-256: e3c6fdaac41e60f2313a440fa1776f3a5fdd16800ff967915e9800985b680822.
The exact-version path dependency ships this repair without an upstream release.

Native changes from that archive:

- `StoreInner::save`: serialize before touching disk, stage in the destination
  directory with installed tempfile, write all bytes, sync the file, persist
  atomically, sync the directory on Unix, then independently read and compare
  committed bytes. No second authoritative cache, journal or legacy-source writer.
- `StoreBuilder::build_inner`: only a genuinely absent file uses defaults; existing
  read/deserialize failures return operation, path and cause before registration.
  Both normal and override-defaults load paths behave this way.
- Saves are explicit by default. No unconditional save on App exit. Upstream's
  opt-in auto-save methods remain available, but migration callers must not use
  them as an acknowledgement. `create_new` still means an explicit forced reset;
  migration callers must use ordinary load, never force defaults over a failure.
- `Error::Storage` carries the filesystem operation, path and original cause.
- The manifest adds tempfile and removes tracing (exit-save logging removed).
  This package is excluded from the application workspace, retaining upstream's
  third-party lint ownership. No global JS injection script is built: roundup
  uses module imports, and `withGlobalTauri` is off. Permission manifests are
  generated by the official build script; no store capability is granted yet.
- Archive lockfile, generated permissions, JS bundle and unrelated package
  documentation are omitted; Rust sources and both upstream licences are retained.

Before atomic replacement, failure/interruption leaves the previous committed
file intact. After replacement, a directory-sync/readback failure refuses
acknowledgement but does not undo or hide valid committed records. The caller
must retain its legacy source and pending work until save succeeds. A process
killed before replacement may leave a non-authoritative temporary file; it is
never loaded as the store. This does not implement #4023's migration or UI.

Observers: `cargo nextest run -p desktop --test s2297a`. The existing Linux lane
runs all observers, with strace syscall failure/interruption and readback faults.
The existing macOS lane runs reopen, invalid-existing recovery, serialization
failure and real partial-write failure (isolated child RLIMIT_FSIZE). No native
window, vendor program, credentials or user data are needed.
